mechanism: Confirmed as written. Core has ONE pair of helpers, rpc/util.cpp:116-140: ParseHashV(v, name) tries uint256::FromHex and, on failure, throws RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER (-8) with either "<name> must be of length 64 (not <len>, for '<hex>')" when the length is wrong or "<name> must be hexadecimal string (not '<hex>')" when the length is right and the characters are not hex; ParseHexV does the same for arbitrary hex. Every hash argument in Core goes through them, so the message always names the argument ("hash", "blockhash", "txid", "parameter 3") and always carries the offending text. Here the only shared piece is the boolean predicate VALID-HEX-HASH-P (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:12-16) plus PARSE-HEX-HASH (:18-26), which returns NIL rather than signalling, and each call site invents its own message: "Invalid block hash" (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:253,529,740), "Invalid txid" (:678, src/rpc/mempool.lisp:233, src/rpc/mining.lisp:1014), "blockhash must be a hex string" (:737,2571), "blockhash must be a hex string of length 64" (:2116), "blockhash must be hexadecimal string" (:2449, no offending text), "Invalid txid <hex>" and "Invalid blockhash" (src/rpc/merkleproof.lisp:171,181), "Invalid input txid" (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:867), "Invalid blockhash" (:101), and in the wallet one shared %WALLET-PARSE-TXID (src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1749-1753, src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:2925) carrying Core's PRE-0.21 wording "txid must be of length 64 (not including any '0x' prefix)". A grep of src/ and tests/ for "must be of length 64 (not" and "must be hexadecimal string (not" returns nothing, so no ParseHashV analogue exists anywhere. getchaintxstats is the one place where the CODE also diverges: src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:1592-1601 calls PARSE-HEX-HASH on the argument and, because that returns NIL for any malformed string, feeds NIL to GET-BLOCK-INDEX-ENTRY and raises RPC_INVALID_ADDRESS_OR_KEY (-5) "Block not found" -- Core reaches ParseHashV first (rpc/blockchain.cpp getchaintxstats) and answers -8.
consequence: Kept at S3. No value is computed wrongly and no request that Core would accept is accepted here or vice versa: every probe below is a REJECTION on both sides, and the well-formed-but-unknown cases agree exactly (getblockheader and getchaintxstats on a 64-hex hash the index does not hold both answer -5 "Block not found", as Core does). What diverges is the diagnosis a caller gets. Two consequences follow. First, eight Core functional assertions compare the message text verbatim and would fail against this node: rpc_blockchain.py:453-454 (getblockheader), :320-321 (getchaintxstats), rpc_rawtransaction.py:164-167 (getrawtransaction blockhash) and :269-271 (createrawtransaction txid), rpc_txoutproof.py:60-64 (gettxoutproof txid and blockhash), mining_prioritisetransaction.py:218-219, rpc_getblockfrompeer.py:69, wallet_basic.py:172-175 (lockunspent). Second, and the only part that is more than cosmetic, getchaintxstats collapses "you sent a malformed blockhash" (-8) into "that block does not exist" (-5): a client that branches on the error class -- retry another node on -5, fix the argument on -8 -- takes the wrong branch, and its own bug is reported as a chain-state fact. That is a wrong diagnosis, not a wrong value, so it does not reach S2 under the money/acted-on-value rule.
evidence: Probe build/ga11v/p-hash.lisp (worktree fix/ga11v-rpcutil-s3a, warm image bitcoin-lisp-dev-e618132ea0cf), every call through bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method on params passed through bl.rpc::%normalize-rpc-params, with Core's own test inputs. Results (ours | Core at d3056bc): getblockheader "nonsense" => -8 "Invalid block hash" | -8 "hash must be of length 64 (not 8, for 'nonsense')"; getblockheader "ZZZ0000...0000" (64 chars) => -8 "Invalid block hash" | -8 "hash must be hexadecimal string (not 'ZZZ0000...')"; getchaintxstats blockhash '0' => -5 "Block not found" | -8 "blockhash must be of length 64 (not 1, for '0')"; getchaintxstats blockhash 'ZZZ0000...' => -5 "Block not found" | -8 "blockhash must be hexadecimal string (not 'ZZZ...')"; gettxoutproof ["00000000000000000000000000000000"] => -8 "Invalid txid 00000000000000000000000000000000" | -8 "txid must be of length 64 (not 32, for '000...')"; gettxoutproof blockhash 32 chars => -8 "Invalid blockhash" | -8 "blockhash must be of length 64 (not 32, for '000...')"; createrawtransaction [{txid:'foo'}] => -8 "Invalid input txid" | -8 "txid must be of length 64 (not 3, for 'foo')"; prioritisetransaction 'foo' => -8 "Invalid txid" | -8 "txid must be of length 64 (not 3, for 'foo')"; getblockfrompeer "1234" => -8 "blockhash must be a hex string" | -8 "hash must be of length 64 (not 4, for '1234')"; getrawtransaction(txid, true, "foobar") => -8 "Invalid blockhash" | -8 "parameter 3 must be of length 64 (not 6, for 'foobar')". Controls that AGREE, so the probe is not reporting a blanket difference: getblockheader on the 64-hex unknown hash Core's rpc_blockchain.py:455 uses => -5 "Block not found" (Core -5 "Block not found"); getchaintxstats blockhash '000...0' (64 zeros) => -5 "Block not found" (Core -5 "Block not found"); a 65-character hash => -8, same code as Core. lockunspent could not be driven on the wallet-less test node (-32601 "Method not found (wallet support is disabled)"), so its divergence is established by reading %WALLET-PARSE-TXID rather than by execution. Files: src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:12-26,253,529,678,737,740,1592-1601,2116,2449,2571; src/rpc/mempool.lisp:230-233; src/rpc/mining.lisp:1014; src/rpc/merkleproof.lisp:171,181; src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:101,867; src/wallet/wallet-tx.lisp:1749-1753; src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:2925; refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/util.cpp:116-140.
fix_shape: Port the two helpers, then convert the call sites; converting sites without the helper is what produced the eleven spellings in the first place. Add PARSE-HASH-V (value name) and PARSE-HEX-V (value name) next to VALID-HEX-HASH-P in src/rpc/blockchain.lisp: each takes the caller's own argument NAME as a string, checks stringp first (Core's get_str throws the RPC_TYPE_ERROR "JSON value of type ... is not of expected type string", which the type gate finding be96017b owns), then signals rpc-error +rpc-invalid-parameter+ with (format nil "~A must be of length 64 (not ~D, for '~A')" name (length s) s) when the length is not 64 and (format nil "~A must be hexadecimal string (not '~A')" name s) when it is 64 but not hex, and otherwise returns the reversed 32-byte vector PARSE-HEX-HASH already builds. Export both from bl.rpc so the wallet files can drop %WALLET-PARSE-TXID onto them. Then replace every site listed above with a call carrying Core's own argument name -- "hash" for getblockheader/getblock/getblockfrompeer, "blockhash" for getchaintxstats/gettxoutproof/getblockstats, "txid" for gettxoutproof entries, createrawtransaction inputs, prioritisetransaction and lockunspent, "parameter 3" for getrawtransaction's blockhash -- taking the name from the corresponding Core call site rather than from the local variable, since Core's names are what its tests assert. getchaintxstats additionally has to call the helper BEFORE the index lookup so the -8 is raised instead of the -5. Ship it with a table-driven test that walks the (method, argument, expected code, expected message) rows Core's eight functional assertions pin, plus the well-formed-unknown-hash rows that must still answer -5, so a regression in either direction is visible.
